parakeet: Let's begin by defining moral superiority, or as I like to call it, moral supremism. Moral superiority is the belief, posture, or performance that says my moral position makes me better than you. It's not the same thing as having strong values. It's not the same thing as believing something is right or wrong. It's not even the same thing as having moral clarity. Moral clarity says this is what I believe is right and this is how I should live. Moral superiority says because I believe what is right, I'm above the people who don't see it the way that I do. That distinction matters. Because morality is supposed to shape how we treat people. But moral superiority takes morality and uses it to measure whether people deserve to be treated with dignity in the first place. At its core, moral superiority says, because I'm right about this issue, I'm above you as a person. And that's where it gets dangerous. Because once morality becomes a ranking system, compassion starts getting replaced by comparison. A person or group identifies a moral issue, takes the correct side of that issue, and then begins measuring everyone else by how closely they conform to the approved position, approved language, approved tone, approved outrage, approved enemies, and approved social performance. And the issue itself may be completely legitimate. Racism is real, abuse, misogyny, religious trauma, homophobia, transphobia, exploitation, corruption, hypocrisy, harm, all of it is real. So the problem is not that people care. The problem is what happens when caring becomes a competition for status. Because moral superiority can take a real concern and turn it into a social weapon. It can take a legitimate harm and use it to justify illegitimate behavior. It can take the desire to reduce harm and mutate it into the desire to be seen as one of the good people. And once that happens, the question shifts. It's no longer are we becoming more responsible? It becomes who gets to stand above whom. That's how moral superiority works. It doesn't usually begin with cruelty, it begins with certainty, then comparison, then performance, then permission. And once that cycle starts, good people can become cruel while believing they're absolutely innocent.
